Forgot to check in a file?  I don't see any handling for TemporaryFileSystem
I've added it in the service file

Like I said on the previous patch, lets add this when moveToPath when and if it's required.  It's still not clear to me what use case requires doing a post-creation copy to a different path.  I understand you have emmc use cases, but I suspect there's simpler designs that involve linking the bmcweb temporary file storage to the appropriate place in the first place. (using systemd TemporaryDirectory)

But there are some pre-checks which needs to be performed in bmcweb before pldm or any other app starts update.
other apps ack on the inotify event which is created when the file is copied to /tmp/images
/tmp/images is on the same device, it doesn't require std::filesystem::copy_file.
Done

This method will be called for the inotify update flow.

Let me take an example of pldm update, In the current PLDM update workflow:
1. BMCWeb performs preliminary validation (checking firmwareUpdateInProgress status, verifying target devices, etc.)
2. Upon successful validation, BMCWeb writes the firmware image from the HTTP request body to /tmp/images
3. PLDM's inotify watch on /tmp/images detects the new file via IN_CLOSE_WRITE event
4. This callback method is invoked to process the firmware package
5. PLDM creates a software object that BMCWeb uses to monitor update progress

With the proposed memory optimization changes, we need to preserve this same workflow.
However, since /tmp/images and /tmp/bmcweb reside on different filesystems, we cannot use filesystem::rename() for an efficient move operation. Using copy_file() would be inefficient as it performs both copy and delete operations, effectively requiring double the package size in available memory. This is why I suggested implementing a meson build option to configure the path.
That's fine, the problem I have is with std::filesystem::copy_file.  These are directories on the same mount, that code will never execute.
Done
Why are we duping the FD here?  This could lead to leaked descriptors.  The name "moveToFd" implies that the element is closed.
Done
Why do we need exec?

I've pushed some changes to this patch, please take a look.

The largest change is that we're now using TemporaryFileHandle that's not a part of DuplicatedFileHandle.  We had a similar class used in test utils that was used for something similar.

Hopefully this patch is closer, even if it doesn't do everything needed.  We have unit test coverage now, so it's good to me.
FYI, this class was doing something very similar.  They're now combined.

I've removed the meson option and the no-lint exception.  The write() calls are blocking, so writing to anything other than tmpfs (as currently written) will cause issues.  We can iterate.
